s.label: SDNQ Attention Hadamard Group Size
s.hint:
Width of the Hadamard rotation in channels. Wider groups mix more channels together and spread outliers further.

Clamped to the head dimension of the running model, rounded down to a power of two that divides it. On a model with 64 or 128 channels per head the upper part of this range resolves to that head dimension rather than to the number shown. Rotation is skipped below 4.
Applies while SDNQ Attention use Hadamard is enabled.

Default 256.

s.label: SDNQ Attention MatMul type
s.hint:
Precision for query-key attention matrix multiplication:
- enabled / int8: 8-bit integer quantization (default)
- float16 / float8_e4m3fn: 8/16-bit float quantization
- disabled: native model precision

s.label: SDNQ Attention PV MatMul type
s.hint:
Precision the probability-value matmul is computed in, the second of the two matmuls in attention. Choices match SDNQ Attention MatMul type.

Quantizing this one as well takes out the floating point work the first setting leaves behind, and it is the more delicate of the two: its inputs are already normalized probabilities, and the small ones among them carry the fine detail.
disabled keeps this matmul in the model's own precision.

Default disabled.

s.label: SDNQ Attention Quantize FP32
s.hint:
Upcasts query, key, and value tensors to FP32 during mean subtraction and scale calculations for better quantization precision.

Improves scale accuracy on BF16 models with negligible performance impact on NVIDIA/AMD GPUs. Enabled by default.

s.label: SDNQ Attention use FP16 Accumulation
s.hint:
Accumulates floating point attention matmuls in FP16 rather than FP32.
Accelerates computation on GPUs with fast FP16 tensor cores. Disabled by default.

s.label: SDNQ Attention use Hadamard
s.hint:
Applies an orthogonal Hadamard rotation matrix to query and key tensors before quantization.
Distributes channel outliers evenly to reduce low-bit quantization artifacts.

Requires SDNQ Attention MatMul type enabled. Disabled by default.

s.label: SDNQ Attention use Smooth K
s.hint:
Subtracts the mean of the keys before quantizing them. Keys carry a large offset that is shared across the sequence, which spends most of the quantized range representing a value identical for every key and leaves little of it for the differences that decide the attention.
Softmax ignores a constant shift applied to every score in a row, so removing that offset changes the quantization error and not the attention.

Costs one mean and one subtraction per call.
Enabled by default.

s.label: SDP kernels

- Memory: memory-efficient attention kernel supporting arbitrary masks

s.label: SDP overrides

- Flex attention: PyTorch compiled flex_attention

s.label: Sparse Attention dense steps
s.hint:
Number of steps at the start and end of sampling that receive a larger budget, where composition and fine detail are set. Counted at each end, and capped at half the run.

Only takes effect when Sparse Attention dense step bonus is above 0.
0 applies one budget to every step.
Default 0.

s.label: Sparse Attention KV budget
s.hint:
Percentage of the eligible key tiles each query tile keeps. Lower budgets are faster and coarser, and the cost shows first in fine detail and in consistency across the image.
Text, conditioning and audio tokens are always kept, as are the tiles on the diagonal, so the budget applies only to the bulk image or video tokens.

100 keeps every tile, which is ordinary dense attention and a convenient comparison run.
Default 30.

s.label: Sparse Attention minimum sequence
s.hint:
Shortest sequence that is sparsified. Below it attention stays dense, because choosing the tiles costs more than skipping them saves.
Sequence length is not resolution: a diffusion transformer sees roughly (width/16) x (height/16) tokens for an image, so 1024x1024 is about 4k tokens and 2048x2048 about 16k, and video multiplies that by the frame count.

0 sparsifies every sequence that reaches the stage.
Default 8192, around 1450x1450 for an image.

Reduces selection overhead on multi-head architectures and prevents banding artifacts on sensitive models. Disabled by default.
